title: FSSAI Mandates New Logo On Milk, Paneer And Ghee Packs From July 2028
seo_title: FSSAI's New Milk Logo Rule For Dairy Packs
meta_description: FSSAI's 6 November 2026 amendment requires a standard blue-and-white logo on milk, paneer, ghee and other dairy packs from 1 July 2028.
court: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
case_name: Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026
citation: Notification dated 6 November 2026, inserting a new provision into Schedule I of the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020
body: On 6 November 2026, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India notified the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026, inserting a new logo requirement into Schedule I of the 2020 Labelling and Display Regulations. The change looks small on paper, a single graphic element, but it touches nearly every dairy pack sold in the country: milk, curd, paneer, ghee, butter, cheese, khoa, ice cream, flavoured fermented milk and composite products built on a dairy base such as fruit shrikhand.

The logo itself is defined with some precision. It is a white drop set inside a blue square, the blue specified by the CMYK formula C89 M58 Y0 K0, and it must sit on the principal display panel of the pack rather than on a side panel or the back. Size depends on how big that panel is. A pack whose principal display panel runs up to 100 square centimetres needs a blue square at least 6 millimetres to a side, with the drop inside it at least 4.56 millimetres high and 3 millimetres wide. Once the panel grows past 100 square centimetres and up to 500, the square must grow to at least 8 millimetres and the drop to at least 6.08 millimetres high and 4 millimetres wide. Reports describe further size bands for larger packaging, but only these two bands could be confirmed across more than one account of the amendment.

None of this is wholly new territory for FSSAI. A draft covering both this logo and a separate set of changes to nutrition labelling went out for public comment in February 2025. What came into force on 6 November 2026 is narrower: it deals only with the dairy logo, leaving whatever became of the nutrition-labelling piece of that same draft to be tracked separately.

Businesses get a long run-up. The logo becomes mandatory from 1 July 2028, nearly twenty months after the notification, which gives dairies, packers and importers time to work the new artwork into their next packaging redesign rather than having to recall or relabel stock already on shelves or in a warehouse. Coverage of the amendment treats the delay as deliberate, consistent with how FSSAI has phased in other packaging changes in the past rather than demanding an overnight switch.

FSSAI's stated reason for the logo is identification rather than safety. Existing food-safety and compositional standards for milk and milk products are untouched by this amendment; what changes is that a shopper picking up a paneer packet in a Kolkata sweet shop or a litre of milk at a Delhi kirana store gets one consistent visual cue, regardless of brand, marking the product as falling within FSSAI's dairy category. That is a labelling device, not a quality certification, and the amendment does not claim to be the latter.

The compliance burden falls unevenly. A large dairy cooperative redesigning a national packaging range absorbs this as one line item in an artwork cycle it was going to run anyway. A small paneer seller or regional dairy running short production lines, the kind common across the dairy belt feeding Delhi and Kolkata, has less slack to get the drop-and-square proportions right across every pack size it sells, and getting them wrong after July 2028 would be a labelling violation under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, separate from and in addition to any question about the product's actual safety or quality.

What is missing from the public record so far is any formal industry response, from dairy cooperatives, trade associations or individual manufacturers, to the final notification. That reaction, once it surfaces, bears watching before the 2028 deadline, since any objection raised now would have to be weighed against the comparatively long lead time FSSAI has already built into the rule.

There is also a practical compliance question that packaging designers will have to work through pack by pack rather than once for an entire product line: a dairy that sells the same product in a 200 ml pouch, a 500 ml carton and a 15-litre institutional pack has to check which size band each format falls into and scale the logo accordingly, rather than carrying one fixed artwork element across the whole range the way a brand logo usually travels. Getting that mapping wrong on even one SKU, while the rest of the range complies, would still leave that single product out of step with the rule once it takes effect.
why_it_matters: Dairy manufacturers, packers and importers selling milk, curd, paneer, ghee, butter, cheese, khoa, ice cream or flavoured fermented milk need to plan a packaging redesign that fits FSSAI's new blue-and-white logo onto the principal display panel at the correct size for each pack format, before the rule takes effect on 1 July 2028. The lead time is long, but getting the square and drop dimensions wrong after that date is a labelling violation distinct from any food-safety defect, so the artwork change deserves its own compliance checklist rather than being folded informally into a routine label update.
card_summary: FSSAI's 6 November 2026 amendment adds a mandatory blue-and-white logo to milk, paneer, ghee, cheese and other dairy packs from 1 July 2028, sized to the pack's display panel.
card_tip: Dairy manufacturers and packers should build the new FSSAI logo into their next packaging redesign now; the rule becomes mandatory on 1 July 2028.
verification_notes: The notification title, its 6 November 2026 date, and the insertion of a new clause into Schedule I of the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 are confirmed by both the SCC Online Blog post and the Corpseed law update, which independently cite the same date and statutory hook; Business Today's 13 November 2026 report confirms the same amendment and adds the 1 July 2028 compliance date, also given by Corpseed and IndiaLaw. The scope (milk, curd, paneer, ghee, butter, cheese, khoa, ice cream, flavoured fermented milk and dairy-based composite products) is taken from Business Today and IndiaLaw, which list the same categories. The logo's colour specification (white drop on a blue square, CMYK C89 M58 Y0 K0) and its placement on the principal display panel are confirmed by a Chemlinked Global Food Compliance report and IndiaLaw. Only the first two size bands (panels up to 100 sq cm, and 100 to 500 sq cm) could be confirmed from more than one source in this run; a reported third and fourth band for larger panels appeared in only one source and has been left out. The February 2025 draft background is taken from a contemporaneous Foodnavigator/Dairyreporter report and the Chemlinked piece, both describing the same draft covering nutrition labelling and the milk logo together. No formal dairy-industry trade body or cooperative response to the final 2026 notification appeared in this run's searches, so none is attributed.
